What a /6 means

A /6 holds 67,108,864 addresses and is only seen as a large provider or registry aggregate.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /6 uses 6 network bits and leaves 26 host bits, so the block contains 67,108,864 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−6) − 2 = 67,108,864 − 2 = 67,108,862.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 0.0.0.1 252.0.0.0
!
access-list 10 permit 0.0.0.0 3.255.255.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 0.0.0.1/6

Linux

ip addr add 0.0.0.1/6 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /6?

67,108,862. A /6 has 67,108,864 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 67,108,862 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /6?

252.0.0.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 3.255.255.255.
